name: Electricity and gas supply

bnote.351101: India's five largest listed coal-based power generators.
bnote.351103: GIPCL runs gas and lignite plants in Gujarat. Vistra and NRG are large US gas-fired generators.
bnote.351104: India's nuclear plants are run by NPCIL, which is not listed. Constellation is the largest listed nuclear operator in the US.
bnote.351201: India's two listed hydro PSUs, then Brookfield Renewable, a global hydro leader.
bnote.351203: Inox Green runs wind-farm operations in India. Ørsted and NextEra are the largest listed wind operators abroad.
bnote.351205: Drax runs the UK's largest biomass power station.
bnote.351303: No listed Indian EV-charging pure-play. These are the largest listed US charging networks.
bnote.352004: Listed Indian city-gas and gas-transmission companies.
bnote.352099: Petronet LNG imports and regasifies LNG. Closest listed match.
bnote.354000: India's power exchange and largest listed power trader.
bnote.352002: No listed green-hydrogen producer yet with meaningful revenue.
bnote.351204: No listed company generates power from green hydrogen at scale yet.

flags.ntpc: Very large net debt, typical of a regulated utility.
flags.adanigreen: Very high P/E; heavy debt-funded growth.
flags.ntpcgreen: Very high P/E for a recently listed company.
flags.inoxgreen: Net profit is above EBITDA, so it includes one-off or other income.
flags.gujgas: The page under the GUJGASLTD ticker shows the name Gujarat Energy. Check the source page.
flags.drax: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.bep: Loss in the trailing year; usual for a growth-focused renewable company.

notes: Section D: utilities are well covered
India has listed companies for coal, hydro, solar, transmission, distribution, city gas and power trading. Nuclear, EV charging and storage use listed companies abroad.
